# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
MISTAKES, mine, in the order they cost the most.

1. THE CEREMONY DID NOT RUN. I archived and reported without producing this pack. The founder
   asked twice and scored it 0 out of 5. The rule was written down, injected at session start,
   and not executed. Knowing a rule is not running it.

2. THE MANIFEST TAX, PAID FOUR TIMES. I resealed CHECKSUMS.sha256 in a tree carrying another
   writer's uncommitted edits, which sealed content that was not in the commit and failed every
   platform. I identified that exact failure, wrote it into the sprint 4 backlog with its
   mechanism, and then did it again two hours later.

3. SEVEN CI ROUND TRIPS FOR INFORMATION ALREADY ON THIS MACHINE. I pushed, waited for five
   platforms, read a log, fixed one class, pushed again. Every failing step was runnable locally
   in under two minutes, and every failing tool named its own remedy in its output. Running the
   whole CI step list locally at the end took ninety seconds and found nothing, which is what it
   should have done at the start.

4. A DISPATCH THAT COULD NEVER HAVE WORKED. I sent implementation work to a read-only reviewer
   agent, which correctly refused. About 41,000 tokens. The agent TYPE is part of the brief.

5. A BRIEF NAMING FILES THAT WERE NOT FREE. I told a builder to write src/brothersbe/contracts.py,
   which already held 423 lines of tested merged code for an unrelated feature. It refused and
   quoted git rather than asserting. Check named files are free before dispatch.

6. TWO WRONG CLAIMS I CAUGHT MYSELF. I compared a list against a string and briefly declared a
   working fix STILL BROKEN. I called a comparison function with raw SQL where it wanted parsed
   values, got character-by-character garbage, and nearly reported it as a new defect. I checked
   the signature first. The second is the exact failure this product exists to refuse: a
   plausible result that would have been wrong to report.

7. I LOST TRACK OF MY WORKING DIRECTORY and wrote a file into a live agent's worktree. Lifted it
   out and left the worktree as I found it.

WHAT WORKED, and should be kept.

- ADVERSARIAL REVIEW EARNED ITS COST TWICE. Both new pieces looked green by their own tests and
  both were NOT SOUND. Roughly 145,000 tokens of review caught two false greens that would have
  shipped. The rule that a verdict counts only when it names the falsification actually executed
  is what made both reports actionable rather than opinion.

- RE-RUNNING SUBAGENT CLAIMS CAUGHT EVERY DEFECT. One builder returned no report at all and its
  work still needed three repairs. A cheap-tier agent reported 67 ageing corrections where the
  measured figure was 62, and ranked a checksum item on a claim that reproduced as zero.

- THE ARCHIVE-BEFORE-RESET HABIT SAVED REAL WORK. A precautionary copy taken three hours earlier
  was the only reason a hard reset was a footnote rather than lost work.

- THE DRIFT HOOKS WERE RIGHT EVERY TIME THEY FIRED, including on wording that read as a
  completion claim when nothing had run.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
